messages:
ana: quick RFC follow-up — we sketched a "matchmaker" layer between router and policy-eval in the last meeting. need to decide the adapter surface so eng/runtime and platform teams can implement without rework. cc @mike_r @sasha :wave:
mike_r: two proposals i sketched earlier: 1) minimal matchmaker: input -> candidate list + score + small hints (est_latency, est_cost, model_variant). very cache-friendly and fast. 2) expressive matchmaker: full policy DSL evaluation inside adapter, returns ranked buckets, metadata, and recommended fallback strategies. more powerful but harder to cache and test.
sasha: +1 on enumerating tradeoffs. also think about determinism for canaries — if we want identical routing semantics across hosted/dedicated/private, the surface must be small and well-versioned.
cheng: practical constraints: private deployments wont allow outbound calls, so adapters must be implementable as local libs or sidecars. that pushes us toward a small RPC-friendly contract, not an embedded DSL.
ana: what about telemetry & explainability? product will need per-request reasons (why candidate chosen) for debugging and audits. can we keep that while keeping surface small?
mike_r: idea: adapter returns short reason codes (enum strings) + optional human-readable explanation limited to ~200 chars. that keeps payload small but queryable. example: `{\n  candidates: [{model: "rw-13b-q4", score: 0.87, est_latency_ms: 72, est_cost: 0.003, reason: "affinity+geo"}],\n  decision_id: "v1.3.2-matchmaker",\n  explain: "affinity to tenant, region match"\n}`
sasha: looks fine. also need a stable tie-breaker: deterministic sort key that includes shard affinity, replica health, and a salt seeded by rollout id. otherwise A/Bs will diverge.
cheng: caching keys: request model, seq_len_histogram_bucket, tenant_id (when allowed), region, policy_version. keep key deterministic and small. recommend TTLs per bucket plus event-driven invalidation on model deploy.
nana: failure modes: what happens if matchmaker adapter returns empty list or errors? we need fallback ordering: 1) fallback_candidates from runtime (precomputed), 2) best-effort default heuristic, 3) fail closed for sensitive tenants. ops-bot: deploy-checker will emit alert if fallback used > 1% per minute.
mike_r: performance budget: matchmaker evaluation must be < 1ms p50 in-path for minimal surface. expressive evaluations can be async — allow matchmaker to return immediate candidates and schedule a background re-rank that patches cache.
sasha: API boundary idea: sync API = quick_rank(request_metadata) -> candidates (required). async API optional: enrich(decision_id) -> updated metadata. ensures low-latency path and better decisions later.
cheng: adapters interface: HTTP/GRPC with proto that uses small enum-coded fields, supports local library shim for private deployments. versioned proto + semantic versioning required.
nana: security: adapters must not leak tenant PII in logs/explain. include a sanitized flag and a sanitized_explain field if needed.
mike_r: tests: unit + integration + perf harness. add golden test vectors for deterministic ordering, and a fuzz runner for weird combos.
sasha: actionable: i can write a short RFC addendum that defines minimal sync surface, explain enums, tie-breaker salt, cache key shape, and failure semantics. cheng — can you draft the proto skeleton for adapter? mike_r — can you prototype the quick_rank shim in runtime sidecar?
cheng: on it. will put a draft proto in repo under infra/matchmaker once we agree on fields.
mike_r: will hack a shim by end of week. perf harness next week.
nana: thanks folks — sounds like a plan. once drafts are up we'll iterate and schedule a gate review. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: NOTE: scheduled follow-up meeting created for 2024-12-05T16:00Z to review addendum and proto.
